subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When a wave refracts on entering a denser medium, which quantity stays constant?
questions.explain: Frequency is determined by the source and is unchanged on refraction; speed and wavelength both decrease.

questions.q: For circular motion, which expression for centripetal acceleration uses angular speed ω?
questions.explain: Since v = ωr, the acceleration v²/r equals ω²r.

questions.q: The relationship between linear speed v and angular speed ω for radius r is:
questions.explain: Linear speed v = ωr.

questions.q: For an object in uniform circular motion, the net (resultant) force is:
questions.explain: The resultant (centripetal) force points toward the centre of the circle.

questions.q: When light reflects off the surface of water, the reflected light becomes partially polarised. This demonstrates that light is:
questions.explain: Only transverse waves can be polarised, so polarisation on reflection confirms light is transverse.

questions.q: An angle of 1 radian corresponds to an arc length equal to:
questions.explain: One radian subtends an arc length equal to the radius.

questions.q: For a simple pendulum of length L, the period of small oscillations is:
questions.explain: The simple pendulum period is T = 2π√(L/g).

questions.q: The refractive index of a medium is defined as:
options: The speed of light in the medium divided by speed in vacuum
The speed of light in vacuum divided by speed in the medium
questions.explain: Refractive index n = c/v, the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the medium.

questions.q: The angular speed ω of an object completing one revolution in period T is:
questions.explain: One revolution is 2π radians, so ω = 2π/T.

questions.q: A pipe open at both ends has length 0.85 m. Taking speed of sound as 340 m/s, what is its fundamental frequency?
questions.explain: For an open pipe λ = 2L = 1.7 m, so f = v/λ = 340/1.7 = 200 Hz.

questions.q: Light damping causes the amplitude of free oscillations to:
questions.explain: With light damping the amplitude decays exponentially while oscillation continues.

questions.q: Increasing the degree of damping on a resonating system causes the resonance peak to:
questions.explain: Greater damping lowers and broadens the resonance peak (and slightly lowers its frequency).

questions.q: The velocity in SHM as a function of displacement x is v = ±ω√(A²−x²). At equilibrium (x=0), the speed is:
questions.explain: At x = 0 the speed is maximum, equal to ωA.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes transverse and longitudinal waves?
options: Both have oscillations perpendicular to energy transfer
In transverse waves oscillations are parallel to energy transfer
In longitudinal waves oscillations are perpendicular to energy transfer
In transverse waves oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
questions.explain: Transverse waves oscillate perpendicular to the direction of energy travel, longitudinal waves oscillate parallel to it.

questions.q: At the point of maximum displacement in SHM, the oscillator has:
questions.explain: At the extremes velocity is zero and acceleration (restoring force) is maximum.

questions.q: Two points on a wave are separated by a path difference of one full wavelength. What is their phase difference?
questions.explain: One whole wavelength corresponds to a phase difference of 360° (2π radians).

questions.q: Using a diffraction grating with d = 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ m and light of wavelength 500 nm, what is the highest order maximum that can be observed?
questions.explain: Maximum n when sinθ ≤ 1: n ≤ d/λ = 1.5×10⁻⁶/500×10⁻⁹ = 3, so n = 3.

questions.q: Unpolarised light passes through two polarising filters whose transmission axes are at 90° to each other. The emergent intensity is:
questions.explain: Crossed polarisers (axes at 90°) block all the light, giving zero transmitted intensity.

questions.q: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and travels at 340 m/s. What is its wavelength?
questions.explain: Using v = fλ, λ = 340/50 = 6.8 m.

questions.q: White light passed through a diffraction grating produces spectra because:
options: All wavelengths diffract by the same angle
Longer wavelengths diffract more than shorter ones
Shorter wavelengths diffract more than longer ones
questions.explain: Since d sinθ = nλ, longer wavelengths (red) are diffracted through larger angles than shorter (violet).

questions.q: At the equilibrium position in SHM, the energy is:
questions.explain: At equilibrium displacement is zero so PE is minimum and KE is maximum.

questions.q: A stationary wave is formed on a string fixed at both ends. The distance between adjacent nodes is:
questions.explain: Adjacent nodes (or antinodes) on a stationary wave are separated by half a wavelength.

questions.q: The total energy of a mass m in SHM with amplitude A and angular frequency ω is:
questions.explain: Total energy E = ½mω²A², equal to the maximum kinetic energy ½m(ωA)².

questions.q: Total internal reflection can occur only when light travels:
options: From a more dense to a less dense medium at an angle above the critical angle
From a less dense to a more dense medium
questions.explain: TIR requires light passing from a higher to a lower refractive index medium at an angle exceeding the critical angle.

questions.q: As an object moves in uniform circular motion, which quantity remains constant?
questions.explain: Speed is constant, but velocity, acceleration and momentum continuously change direction.

questions.q: In SHM, the acceleration is always directed:
questions.explain: The restoring acceleration always points back toward the equilibrium position.

questions.q: Monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm strikes a grating with d = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m. At what angle does the first-order maximum appear?
A 0.50 kg ball moves in a horizontal circle of radius 2.0 m at 4.0 m s⁻¹. The centripetal force is:
For two coherent waves to interfere destructively, the path difference must be:
options: A whole number of wavelengths, nλ
An odd number of half wavelengths, (n + ½)λ
questions.explain: Destructive interference occurs when the path difference is an odd number of half-wavelengths, (n+½)λ.

questions.q: In SHM, the maximum acceleration of an oscillator of amplitude A is:
questions.explain: Maximum acceleration a_max = ω²A, occurring at maximum displacement.
